strokes.text: Import binds an object that already exists in OBS to a resource in your configuration.
It reads the object and does not write the configuration for you.
Procedure
Write the resource block with the values the object has now.
Look up the UUIDs and scene item IDs that the import ID needs.
Run `terraform import` with the whole ID in single quotes, because it contains pipe characters.
Run `terraform plan` and settle every difference deliberately before the first apply.
Import IDs
@resources/scene: `collection|scene_uuid`.
@resources/source, @resources/input and @resources/media_input: `collection|input_uuid|anchor_scene_uuid|anchor_item_id`.
@resources/scene_item: `collection|scene_uuid|source_uuid|item_id`, with `|group` appended for a group.
@resources/group: `collection|scene_uuid|group_uuid|item_id`.
@resources/group_source and @resources/group_input: `collection|scene_uuid|group_uuid|group_item_id|input_uuid|item_id`.
@resources/group_graph: `collection|scene_uuid|group_uuid|parent_item_id|stable_key=source_uuid:item_id,...`.
@resources/filter and the Move filters: a JSON object, shown on each resource page.
@resources/color_filter: collection, parent UUID, parent name and filter name, separated by pipe characters.
Finding UUIDs and Item IDs
obs-websocket reports all of them: `GetSceneList` returns scene UUIDs, `GetInputList` returns source UUIDs and `GetSceneItemList` returns scene item IDs.
Any obs-websocket client can send those requests.
What Import Does Not Do
It never adopts an object by name: an object with the same name and another UUID is a different object.
An imported @resources/source or @resources/filter starts with no managed settings, and the first apply takes ownership of the keys you list.
@resources/scene_contents, @resources/plugin and @resources/collection_seed cannot be imported; declare them and apply.
Adding @resources/scene_contents to an imported scene removes every placement that its list leaves out.
